trap-superlative.evidence: 'Thus, c_k^(lambda) **is** the k-th Ohtsuki invariant of F'; 'This **forms the canonical home** of the rungs'; '**We refute** the real-x archimedean closure of c_3'; '1. Kashiwara crystal (**the load-bearing anchor**)'.
trap-superlative.notes: REPORT ONLY. (1) 'We refute the real-x archimedean closure of c_3' is a durable refutation with NO (a)/(b) scope classification, which AGENTS.md STRICT requires before writing 'refuted / ruled out' in a content block. As it happens the corpus DOES hold a qualifying invariant for this one -- the dc_3/dq ~ 4.6e6 smoothness argument (PR #1821) -- so the fix is to cite it and label the claim scope (b), not to weaken it. (2) TECHNICAL DEFECT in anchor 1: 'For each irreducible representation V_lambda of U_q(sl_n) (and hence H_n(q)), the Kashiwara crystal B(lambda) contains dim V_lambda vertices (one per standard Young tableau)'. These are two different modules with two different dimensions. B(lambda) for U_q(sl_n) has one vertex per SEMIstandard Young tableau -- for lambda = (2,1) over sl_3 that is 8 -- while one vertex per STANDARD tableau is f^lambda = 2, the dimension of the H_3(q)-irrep. The drawing that follows shows 2 vertices, so the block is using the H_n(q)/SYT picture under the U_q(sl_n) crystal's name. Proposed: state it as the standard-tableau basis of the Specht module V_(2,1) of H_3(q), with the f-tilde_1 edge as the crystal-theoretic image. (3) 'This forms the canonical home' is the forms-for-is verb substitution again. EVERYTHING IN SECTION 3 IS EXEMPLARY and should not be re-flagged.
